11,g036,20261102T104200Z-http-dev,"Which fasteners does RF-2 use, and why those?","RF-2 uses stainless steel A4 fasteners because they resist chlorides from salt and are suitable for systems rated up to C4, which matches the corrosionivity category of RF-2.","## Stainless steel fasteners
Aluminium systems use stainless steel fasteners:
- A2 stainless steel is used in systems rated up to C3.
- A4 stainless steel is used in systems rated C4 and above, because it resists chlorides from salt better.
## Choosing between similar products

- **GF-1 or GF-2.** Both are ground-mount systems. GF-2 is rated for C5 and is chosen for coastal sites within 10 km of the sea and for sites near chemical plants. GF-1 is rated for C4 and is used at other sites.
- **RF-1 or RF-2.** Both are ballasted flat-roof systems. RF-2 puts less load on the roof and is rated for C4. RF-1 gives more energy per module because of its south-facing tilt.
The final choice is made in the preliminary design, after the site survey.
## Notes
- RF-2 fits about 20% more modules on the same roof area than RF-1.
- It is the usual choice for roofs with a low load reserve.
- RF-2 needs a positive roof assessment before installation.
# RoofFlat RF-2 east-west ballasted system
RF-2 is a flat-roof system with modules facing east and west in pairs. The low tilt and closed shape catch less wind, so it needs less ballast than RF-1.

The company does not offer any system for category CX.","## What the category means for the product choice
Every mounting system is rated for one maximum category. A system can be used at sites with that category or a lower one. The company does not offer any system for category CX.
# Corrosivity categories
The corrosivity category describes how aggressive the air at a site is to metal. The company uses the categories from ISO 9223.
## How the category of a site is decided

The engineer decides the category during the site survey, using the distance to the sea, nearby industry, the wind direction and visible corrosion on nearby metal structures. When the site is between two categories, the higher one is used.

26,g037,20261102T103932Z-pipeline-dev,"Our plot borders a fertiliser works. Which ground system would you use, and what protects it from rusting?","GroundFrame GF-2 would be used, and its zinc-magnesium coating protects it from rusting.","## Thin but stronger coating

The zinc-magnesium coating on GF-2 is thinner than the hot-dip galvanising on GF-1, but it protects better in salty air. Coating thickness alone does not show which system resists corrosion better; the corrosivity category does.
## Where it is used
- Coastal sites within 10 km of the sea.
- Sites near chemical plants, fertiliser storage or other sources of aggressive air.
- Sites with high snow loads, up to 3.5 kN/m².
# Coatings and materials
## Steel systems

- **Hot-dip galvanising.** Used on GroundFrame GF-1 and CarportFrame CP-1. Parts are galvanised after cutting and drilling, so the edges and holes are also protected. Average coating thickness: 85 µm.

- **Zinc-magnesium coating.** Used on GroundFrame GF-2. The coating is applied to the steel strip before forming. Cut edges are protected by the coating itself, which flows over them as it corrodes slowly. Coating thickness: 25 µm per side.
Bolts and nuts on steel systems are hot-dip galvanised.

30,g038,20261102T103932Z-pipeline-dev,What do we need to have sorted on our land before your crew turns up to build?,"A geotechnical survey, including soil drilling, pull-out tests on sample posts, and a check for groundwater and frost depth, must be completed before the crew turns up to build.","## Geotechnical survey
Every ground-mount project needs a geotechnical survey before the detailed design. It includes:
- soil drilling to describe the soil layers,
- pull-out tests on sample posts,
- a check for groundwater and frost depth.
There are at least 3 pull-out tests per site and at least 1 per MWp of plant size.
The survey is ordered by the company from a partner laboratory. Its cost is part of the commercial offer.
## What the engineer checks
- Site boundaries, access for trucks and machines, and storage space.
- Shading from buildings, trees and terrain.
- For roofs: roof type, slope, condition of the waterproofing, and access to the roof.
- For ground-mount sites: terrain slope, drainage and signs of stony soil.
- Distance to the sea and to industrial plants, to decide the corrosivity category of the site.
## What the design includes
- Layout of rows or roof fields, with the module positions.
- Structural calculation for the wind load and snow load at the site.
- Choice of foundation for ground-mount projects, based on the geotechnical survey.
- Assembly drawings and a bill of materials.
